messages:
maria: drift-detector just flagged a config delta between prod and staging nodepool tags. looks like the Helm values for gpuNodeSelector changed in staging and the reconciler tried to apply it to prod :grimacing:
infra-bot: ALERT: env-drift-reconciler started remediation run 2201123581-rl. 2 nodes cordoned, 6 pods evicted (gpu intensive). see: https://console/reconciler/runs/2201123581
sam: omg — which chart/version?
maria: chart: runtime/nodepool v2.4.1 -> in staging values.gpu.selector: { "nvidia.com/gpu": "present" } but prod still expects label gpu=enabled. rendering bug in our overlay template I think.
tyler: so autopatcher applied the new selector and kube-scheduler removed pods that didn't match? that explains evictions.
jess: :eyes: we should suppress the reconcile until we fix the template. can we patch the reconciler to skip nodepool nodeSelector diffs for gpu pools for 1 hour?
leo: temporary suppress looks fine, but want a careful rollback plan. doing a suppress will leave prod divergent. need to record auditable ticket and follow-up PR.
maria: agreed. plan: 1) suspend drift reconciler job for "gpu-nodepools" via gitops skip annotation; 2) patch nodes back to previous label to get pods stable; 3) open fix PR against chart overlay; 4) re-run dry-run then re-enable reconciler. cost tradeoff: leaving extra reserved capacity vs risk of evictions.
sam: can we do a targeted kubectl patch to re-add label so pods come back without full node recycle?
tyler: yes — command: ```kubectl label nodes <node-name> gpu=enabled --overwrite``` or patch via jsonmerge: ```kubectl patch node <node> -p '{"metadata":{"labels":{"gpu":"enabled"}}}'```
jess: I'll add the gitops skip annotation to the helmrelease: ```metadata:
  annotations:
    reconciler.redwood.ai/skip: "true"```
infra-bot: NOTE: skipping reconciler for helmrelease runtime-nodepool-prod until 2201123900 set by @jess
leo: i'm going to run a small probe after label patch to ensure pods reschedule: ```kubectl get pods -n runtime -o wide | grep gpu```
maria: also check autoscaler minSize in Terraform — staging had min 6, prod 3; if nodes get cordoned we may need to bump min temporarily. cost hit ~+$1.2k/day if we double reserved. preferences?
jess: prefer label patch first, bump min only if patch doesn't stabilize within 10m.
tyler: agree. I'll monitor scheduler logs: ```kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-scheduler-... | grep 'FailedScheduling'```
sam: opened ticket INF-6782 to track this and link the PR. tagging @oncall for visibility.
maria: executing label patch now on the two cordoned nodes, then uncordon. will update thread.
leo: :thumbsup: ping when pods are Running. I'll prepare the overlay fix PR and CI test.
maria: patch done, uncordoned one node, pods are restarting. 4/6 gpu pods back to Running. still 2 Pending, investigating affinity mismatch.
tyler: Pending because tolerations missing on the pod spec after rendering — another template hole. we should run a repo-wide values lint before re-enabling reconcile.
jess: created PR runtime/overlay#452 that fixes selector + tolerations + adds unit test in helmfile. CI passed on staging.
maria: once PR merges we'll re-enable reconciler. recommend setting reconciler to dry-run mode for one reconcile cycle to observe no further evictions.
infra-bot: INFO: reconciler dry-run scheduled at 2201123920 for runtime-nodepool-prod
sam: good. document follow-ups: INF-6782 (incident), PR-452 (fix), and a postmortem runbook to ensure nodeSelector changes require canary scope and not global apply.
maria: thanks all — closing immediate incident. will leave skip annotation until PR merged and dry-run OK. :white_check_mark:
